overclaims: The study compares GPT3 and GPT3.5; this assessment verifies Marcus's account of the research, not a universal causal effect of human feedback.
checks.note: Proposition turns 'made things worse' into 'made it [covert racism] worse'. The contract and evidence both say covert prejudice did not rise significantly, so this says more than Marcus committed to. The limitation naming GPT3 vs GPT3.5 has no support in the evidence: the context names GPT3.5 and GPT4 as the HF-trained models, and t(16) points to a wider comparison. The e1 excerpt is cut to 'neither scaling nor training with human feedback', which drops 'resolve the dialect prejudice' and leaves the quote with no meaning.
